all schools collect data, but few have a deliberate process to evaluate data, and almost none use the data to improve the quality of the experiential education program.

the majority of the programs are not using the best practices for quality assurance in experiential education.
QA for EE in US schools of pharmacy remains largely in the early stages, but that a six-step process for quality improvement (QI) of EE programs has been proposed.
QA practices for experiential education in pharmacy programs are not well defined or standardized.

QA for EE should be an ongoing process that is not limited to a single point in time.
